title: Time 5: по понедельникам, утром (how often, when of day)
titleRussian: Время 5: по понедельникам, утром (как часто, время суток)
description: For something that repeats on certain days, use по + dative plural: по понедельникам (on Mondays). For the parts of the day use NO preposition - just the instrumental: утром, днём, вечером, ночью. 'Every day' is каждый день in the accusative.
descriptionRussian: Для того, что повторяется в определённые дни, используют по + дательный множественного: по понедельникам. Для частей суток предлог не нужен — только творительный падеж: утром, днём, вечером, ночью. «Каждый день» — это каждый день в винительном.
intro: The difference between one Monday and every Monday is a whole different preposition and case, which English marks with nothing at all. Parts of the day work differently again: no preposition and a bare instrumental, which you already met as frozen adverbs in the instrumental book. Three ways to say when, none of them interchangeable.
rules: For recurring days ('on Mondays'), use по + dative plural: по понедельникам, по средам, по выходным.
Compare with Lesson 2: в понедельник = one specific Monday; по понедельникам = every Monday (a routine). The plural -ам / -ям marks repetition.
For parts of the day, use NO preposition - just the instrumental: утром, днём, вечером, ночью.

Don't confuse утром with часов утра from Lesson 1. Утром is a when-tag meaning 'in the morning' (instrumental, stands alone). Часов утра means '... in the morning' after a clock hour (genitive): семь часов утра = seven in the morning. // Не путайте «утром» и «часов утра» из урока 1. «Утром» — это ответ на «когда» (творительный, без числа). «Часов утра» ставится после числа часов (родительный): семь часов утра.
For 'every,' use каждый + accusative, agreeing in gender: каждый день, каждое утро, каждую неделю, каждый год.
Set phrases: по выходным (on weekends), по будням (on weekdays).
examples: По понедельникам у меня спорт. (On Mondays I have sports.) по + dative plural = recurring.
По субботам мы отдыхаем. (On Saturdays we rest.) по субботам.
Утром я пью кофе. (In the morning I drink coffee.) bare instrumental, no preposition.
Вечером мы гуляем. (In the evening we go for a walk.) вечером.
Каждый день я встаю рано. (Every day I get up early.) каждый день, accusative.
Каждую неделю у нас урок. (Every week we have a lesson.) каждую неделю, feminine -у.

tables.title: One day (в + acc) vs every such day (по + dat pl)
Parts of the day: bare instrumental (no preposition)

items.hint: This is a routine, every Monday, not one specific Monday.
items.explanation: For a recurring day use по + dative plural: по понедельникам. В понедельник would mean one specific Monday, not the weekly routine.

items.promptEnglish: In the morning I drink coffee.
items.hint: Parts of the day take no preposition - just one special form.
items.explanation: Parts of the day use the bare instrumental, with no preposition: утром ('in the morning'). 'В утро' is wrong; the instrumental утром does the whole job.

items.promptEnglish: Every day I get up early.
items.hint: Каждый agrees with день, which is masculine.
items.explanation: Каждый agrees in gender with its noun. День is masculine, so каждый день. (Compare каждое утро, каждую неделю.)

items.hint: По takes the dative PLURAL for recurring days.
items.explanation: Recurring days use по + dative plural: по субботам ('on Saturdays'). The singular субботу (accusative) would be for в субботу, one specific Saturday.

items.promptEnglish: In the evening we walk in the park.
items.hint: Same pattern as утром: bare instrumental.
items.explanation: Like утром, the word for 'in the evening' is the bare instrumental вечером, with no preposition.

items.promptEnglish: Every week we have a Russian lesson.
items.hint: Неделя is feminine -а. Каждый must agree with it in the accusative.
items.explanation: Каждый agrees with its noun. Неделя is feminine, so the accusative is каждую неделю. (Masculine: каждый день; neuter: каждое утро.)

blanks: По _____ я хожу в бассейн. (On Wednesdays I go to the pool.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Recurring days take по + dative plural: по средам ('on Wednesdays'). The singular среду (accusative) belongs to в среду, one specific Wednesday.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each time word into the pattern it follows.

errorCorrection.explanation: For a recurring day ('on Sundays', every Sunday) Russian uses по + the dative PLURAL: по воскресеньям. The form воскресенье is the accusative singular, which belongs to в воскресенье ('on one specific Sunday').

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: At night it is quiet outside.
errorCorrection.explanation: Parts of the day are expressed with the bare instrumental and no preposition: ночью ('at night'). Ночь is the nominative dictionary form, which cannot stand alone to mean 'at night'.
Каждый agrees in gender with its noun in the accusative. Утро is neuter, so 'every morning' is каждое утро. Каждый is the masculine form (каждый день), wrong for the neuter утро.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: On Mondays I go to the gym.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'On Mondays' (every Monday, a routine) is по понедельникам, with по + dative plural. В понедельник would mean one specific Monday, not the weekly habit.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: In the evening I drink tea.
minimalPairs.explanation: Parts of the day take the bare instrumental with no preposition: вечером. 'В вечер' is not how Russian marks the time of day.

reviewVocab.definition: the pattern for recurring days: по понедельникам, по средам, по выходным. It means 'every such day,' unlike в + accusative for one specific day.
the bare instrumental adverbs for parts of the day; no preposition is used.
reviewVocab.example: Утром я пью кофе, а вечером чай.

reviewVocab.definition: 'every'; каждый agrees in gender with its noun in the accusative: каждый день, каждое утро, каждую неделю.
